A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CountGD++ and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. Corresponding content can be matched despite appendix renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original CountGD++ counting and detection experiments across multiple datasets, including prompt comparisons, an attention ablation, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds CARPK evaluation and normalized-count results on FSCD-147.

M1.justification: v2 adds a separately evaluated inference variant applying SAM test-time normalization from CountGD to counts when internal exemplars are provided. The original direct box-counting variant remains. The architecture, training losses, negative prompting, pseudo-exemplar procedure, and adaptive cropping are unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds CARPK evaluation on 459 drone images of parking-lot cars, without fine-tuning (Sections 6.1 and A.2). This adds an aerial-image domain to the existing counting coverage. All previously evaluated datasets and tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The new CARPK comparison in Table A.2 includes CounTX and VLCounter, which were discussed but not evaluated in v1. CLIP-Count, CountGD, and CountSE also appear there. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds normalized-count evaluation for the internal-exemplar FSCD-147 settings, alongside the original box-count results; detection AP/AP50 use boxes unaffected by normalization. The new CARPK evaluation uses the prompt 'car' and three automatically selected pseudo-exemplars. Existing training settings and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Table A.3 adds a comparison of counts with and without test-time normalization in two fixed FSCD-147 prompt settings, showing its effect on counting error. The existing attention ablation, cropping examples, MLLM diagnostics, and qualitative cases are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed analysis, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added results follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds CARPK MAE/RMSE of 2.48/3.74 and normalized FSCD-147 results of 6.43/32.73 for exemplars only and 5.86/18.79 for text plus exemplars; the original unnormalized rows remain. All four CountGD++ Fruits rows in Table 2 change. For positive/negative internal exemplars, MAE/RMSE changes from 0.56/1.24 to 0.41/1.51 and AP/AP50 from 0.69/0.92 to 0.62/0.83. These mixed revisions have no accompanying explanation or stated setting change. Other benchmark results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The inference inequalities, training-loss formulation, matching cost, and mathematical reasoning are unchanged. The normalization addition introduces no new mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: negative prompting, automatic pseudo-exemplars, external natural or synthetic exemplars, and use as an LLM counting expert. Added benchmark evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains that normalization helps avoid double counting but does not improve the output boxes, qualifying how counting improvements relate to localization. Its expanded FSCD-147 discussion also distinguishes density-based counts from direct box enumeration. Existing limitations and other mechanism interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Section A.3 explicitly documents adaptive cropping across FSCD-147 prompt settings, normalization applicability, and which outputs underlie counting versus detection metrics. CARPK prompting and exemplar details are also supplied. Training details and resource-access statements remain unchanged; the code URL only gains a trailing slash.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hsieh et al.'s 2017 drone-based counting paper as the CARPK reference. Existing related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantively unchanged; most citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a CARPK appendix subsection, expands the FSCD-147 output-mode explanation, and updates dataset descriptions and cross-references. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the CARPK table and expands the FSCD-147 table with two shaded normalization rows and a longer explanatory caption. Tables and appendix figures are locally relocated. Figure A.3 changes the annotation 'y = 40' to 'Predicted Count = 40'; its plotted evidence is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added CARPK test modestly strengthens evidence for transfer to drone imagery. Separating normalized counts from direct box counts and explaining their relationship to detection metrics improves interpretability. These are limited gains to an otherwise stable paper. The unexplained, mixed Fruits revisions still prevent conclusions about why those reported values changed.
